rules: A win resets the loss ladder to 1,900, so the round after a win is often the poorest.

Attackers who lose, survive and did not plant, and defenders who lose and survive after the spike goes off, are paid 1,000 flat with no loss bonus. Surviving a lost round therefore costs 900 to 1,900 credits.
Saving only pays when the gun kept is worth more than the bonus given up: a rifle always, a Spectre about break-even at the 2,900 tier, a pistol never.
Survive and your weapon and armor carry over. Die and you keep any bought-but-unused abilities but lose the gun.
Everything resets to 800 at halftime, so unspent credits in the last round of a half are burned.
Overtime resets every player to 5,000 each round.

armor.name: Light Shield
armor.note: Absorbs 66% of damage until spent. Buys about one extra bullet against SMGs and rifles; changes no headshot outcome.

armor.name: Regen Shield
armor.note: Absorbs 100% until broken, then refills after a gap. Better than heavy for anchors taking separate fights, worse for one sustained duel. Consensus is soft.

armor.name: Heavy Shield
armor.note: Against a Vandal or a close Phantom, light and heavy are both four body shots. It pays against 26-35 damage weapons and against headshots in the 125-150 band.

weapons.name: Ghost
weapons.note: Best eco pistol at low ranks: one-taps an unshielded head to 30m and a 13-round magazine forgives misses.

weapons.name: Bandit
weapons.note: One-taps light shields to 30m and heavy inside 10m. Eight rounds punishes spray.

weapons.name: Sheriff
weapons.note: The only sub-1,000 gun that one-taps through heavy shields inside 30m. Below Gold a Ghost plus shield and utility is usually worth more.

weapons.name: Bucky
weapons.note: Per pellet under 8m. Close-corner anchor buy.

weapons.name: Marshal
weapons.note: Best pure-eco primary: 101 body kills an unshielded enemy outright, and players on an anti-eco often skip shields.

weapons.name: Stinger
weapons.note: Only worth the 500 saved over a Spectre if the fight is inside 15m.

weapons.name: Spectre
weapons.note: The default half-buy gun at every rank.

weapons.name: Ares
weapons.note: Under-bought at low ranks: a machine gun on an SMG budget, 50 rounds and strong wall penetration.

weapons.name: Judge
weapons.note: Per pellet under 10m. Full-buy money on a half-buy budget; wins its intended fight and loses every other one.

weapons.name: Bulldog
weapons.note: The safer of the two sub-rifle options at low ranks.

weapons.name: Guardian
weapons.note: One-taps through heavy at any range, but three body shots through heavy. A skill check.

weapons.name: Outlaw
weapons.note: One body shot kills through no shield and light, but leaves a heavy-shielded target at 10 HP. That is the whole decision.

weapons.name: Phantom
weapons.note: Silenced, 30 rounds, 11 shots a second. Past 20m a headshot leaves a heavy-shielded enemy at 10 HP and body shots go from four to five. Favours close angles and messy spray.

weapons.name: Vandal
weapons.note: One-taps through heavy at any range and four body shots at any range. Favours long sightlines.

weapons.name: Warden
weapons.note: Added in patch 13.06. Two body shots unshielded, three through any shield, at 6.5 shots a second. Too new for a verdict: do not tell the player it is right or wrong to buy.

weapons.name: Odin
weapons.note: A wallbang specialist that costs more than a rifle and loses most open duels.

weapons.name: Operator
weapons.note: Needs the team near the credit cap, because the buyer cannot also afford utility and needs teammates covering flanks.

buy_types.name: Full buy
buy_types.shape: Rifle 2,900 plus heavy shield 1,000. 4,400 to 4,900 is the real target once abilities are included; 3,900 is a full buy only if utility carried over from last round.

buy_types.name: Half buy
buy_types.shape: Spectre 1,600 plus light shield 400 is exactly 2,000. Other shapes: Marshal plus heavy, Bulldog plus light plus one ability, Sheriff plus heavy plus utility.

buy_types.name: Force buy
buy_types.shape: Spending everything below the full-buy line on purpose. Gated on being at the 2,400 tier or higher, four of five able to afford a gun and some shield, and the enemy not on a full buy.

buy_types.name: Eco
buy_types.shape: Spend 500 or less. Classic or Ghost, maybe one ability, usually no shield. The point is that all five clear 3,900 next round.

buy_types.name: Bonus
buy_types.shape: The round after winning an eco, carrying picked-up enemy rifles. Buy shields and utility only and bank the 2,900 you would have spent on a gun.

priorities: Buy with the team or do not buy. Five Spectres beat one Vandal and four Classics; a lone rifle inside a team eco is one kill reward for the enemy and a free gun when they pick it up.
If fewer than three of five can afford a primary and a shield, the round is an eco whatever the player personally holds.
On a half buy, light shield plus a better gun plus utility beats heavy shield plus a worse gun. On a full buy heavy is correct, because the 600 is no longer competing with anything.

Abilities beat the armor upgrade when the ability creates or denies a fight: a smoke across an Operator sightline, a flash that turns a duel into a free kill, recon that prevents walking into three people.
Never buy a rifle with no shield and no utility on a full-buy round.
An attacker taking a site wants the gun first; a defender anchoring a close site wants shield and utility first.
Read the enemy economy. Full-buying with heavy shields into an obvious enemy eco wastes credits that should have been saved.
Check MIN NEXT ROUND in the buy menu. That number is the game telling you whether saving works.
dropping: The poorer player right-clicks the weapon they want, which posts a Request beside their name; a richer teammate right-clicks the same weapon to buy it for them.
Buying for someone who has not requested does not work through the menu. The fallback is buying a second gun and pressing G near them.
A requested weapon keeps the receiver's skin; a dropped one carries the dropper's. A weapon dropped with G can no longer be refunded.
Drop from the biggest surplus to the most gun-dependent role. Dropping to a player who will lurk passively is a waste.
Sitting near the 9,000 cap while teammates are under-equipped is hoarding: those credits should have been guns.
